The relationship between the radiographic transition zone and the level of aganglionosis in Hirschsprung's disease has not been found to be strongly correlated. While there is some variation in the extent of transition zone appearance, systematic preoperative biopsy by coelioscopy or ombilical incision is still considered mandatory for accurate assessment.

This correlation between radiographic transition zone and aganglionosis level may not hold true for all patients, as individual variations exist. It's also essential to note that imaging alone cannot provide a definitive diagnosis of Hirschsprung's disease, as the extent of aganglionosis can vary significantly among affected individuals.

Therefore, it is crucial to rely on other diagnostic methods, such as biopsy and clinical evaluation, for an accurate diagnosis and treatment plan in patients suspected of having Hirschsprung's disease.
